text:
Ireland is not part of England. The island is split between the Republic of Ireland, a fully independent country, and Northern Ireland, which is one of the four countries of the United Kingdom alongside England, Scotland, and Wales. The confusion comes from history: England conquered and ruled Ireland from the 12th century, and the island was under British rule until the southern part broke away in 1922 and became a republic in 1949.
